notes: Seven web searches ran; none was refused. Deseret News report on the 29 September 2026 Utah 1st District debate (https://www.deseret.com/politics/2026/09/29/utah-1st-congressional-district-debate-focuses-on-ai-data-centers-and-republican-party-after-trump/) paraphrases him: Congress has not ensured the coming AI disruption benefits all Americans; he wants strong federal guardrails; data centers must not take water from the Great Salt Lake watershed and should not rely on subsidies; he said a roughly $1 million pro-AI PAC spend for him (Think Big, reported as $450,000 in the primary) won't affect his commitment to constrain the industry. These are paraphrase or fragments, so left out of statements; all level D in any case. KSL (11 June 2026) and Deseret News (9 June 2026) report he disclosed owning stock in an AI data center under construction in Delta, Utah. Axios Q&A of 25 June 2026 returned 403 and could not be read. Campaign site priorities page has no AI content. As a non-member he did not sponsor the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act and no source shows he endorsed it. The op-ed quote was read through a page-fetch tool that summarises pages; reviewer should confirm exact wording.
